content: Obesity is a risk factor for the development of several cancers, including breast, colon, and gynecologic carcinomas.^1,2 Recently, it has become clear that obesity is not only associated with carcinogenesis but also influences the prognosis of patients with several types of cancer. For example, obesity has been associated with a poor prognosis in breast^3,4 and colon cancers,^5,6 whereas favorable prognoses have been reported in obese patients with gastric^7 or renal cancers.^8
